clue.text: Put a line beneath nineteen at most?

definitions.meaning: to underline a word on the page
a score is twenty, so nineteen or fewer is below a score

explanation.surface: Someone is told to draw a line under a number no bigger than nineteen.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so any number up to nineteen is 'under score', the second reading split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline text is to draw a rule beneath it; the second reading is a playful split of the word.

clue.text: The language our duchess uses!

indicators.note: the phrase our duchess employs, that is contains within its letters, the name sought

explanation.surface: An exclamation about which tongue a titled lady speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' signals that the letters sit inside 'our duchess', across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: The national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Quick movement with trade mostly on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
most of the word trade is kept, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A sudden surge in business that is mostly rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TRADE to TRAD; 'on the up' turns that round to give the answer, since in a down entry rising means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash or sudden rapid motion, as when someone darts across a road.

clue.text: Sound of burrowing animal in groove

indicators.note: the clue says the word is to be heard, giving a different spelling of the same pronunciation

parts.note: a rabbit lives in a warren of burrows

explanation.surface: Noise from a creature digging underground in a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbet is a woodworking term: a step-shaped recess cut along an edge to take another piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry, a rebate or slot cut into timber to receive a joining part.

clue.text: What quite wrongly makes someone see red?

definitions.text: What quite wrongly makes someone see red?

parts.words: What quite wrongly makes someone see red?
parts.note: seeing red usually means getting angry, but here it is literal: a condition of the eyes in which hues are mistaken, so a person might wrongly perceive green as red

explanation.surface: Asking what unfairly makes a person furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see red' looks like the idiom for losing your temper; read literally it is about perceiving a hue wrongly, a defect of vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision deficiency in which a person cannot tell certain hues apart, such as reds and greens.

clue.text: Part of eye that could have tear in? Yes and no

indicators.note: the letters of tear in could be rearranged into the answer, a hint that they become something else

explanation.surface: Asking whether a part of the eye might be ripped, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is a wink: the retina can indeed suffer a tear, but the answer only 'has tear in' as rearranged letters, not literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eyeball.

clue.text: Was terribly black — has become cleaner

indicators.note: done terribly, the word was is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something that was dreadfully dirty has turned into a cleaning item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges WAS into SWA, and B for black is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad or mop used for wiping and mopping, for instance a ship's deck or a wound.

clue.text: You and I having g-got knowledge like an overdue rest?

parts.note: the pair speaking together are we
acquired knowledge is learned; the stammered g-got tells you to stammer the word too, doubling its first letter

explanation.surface: A stuttering speaker says that they have gained knowledge, like a long-awaited break.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'g-got' is the signal to stammer the word for knowledge acquired, doubling its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A break that has been fully deserved after hard work is said to be merited in this way.

clue.text: Weapon from part of Norfolk with message on base

indicators.note: in a down clue the message sits under the first piece, forming its foundation

parts.note: the Broads are the network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk, an English county
to send word is to send a message

explanation.surface: A weapon is sent from an area of eastern England with a note attached at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are waterways in eastern England; WORD comes beneath BROADS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sword with a wide blade, used for cutting rather than thrusting.

clue.text: New dairy built — with quality of something built to last

definitions.text: quality of something built to last

indicators.note: a new version of dairy built has its letters set out afresh

explanation.surface: A freshly constructed dairy that is made to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the signal to rearrange DAIRY BUILT; the second 'built' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The capacity to withstand wear and remain sound over a long time.

clue.text: Singer from local town

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words local town, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A vocalist who comes from a nearby community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters within 'local town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with a low female or high male voice, the part between soprano and tenor.

clue.text: Prudent management and thrift in state capital

definitions.meaning: an old sense of foresight and careful economy
the capital city of Rhode Island in the USA

explanation.surface: Careful budgeting and saving in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides divine care, the word once meant careful foresight and economy, the root of 'provident'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight and economy in managing resources; also the chief city of Rhode Island, a US state.

clue.text: In a tricky situation, being stuck in the wood?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being in difficulty
literally perched high in a eucalyptus, trapped among its branches

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble, as if trapped in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom, chiefly British and Australian, means in a fix; read literally it is being up in a eucalyptus.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being in a predicament, taken literally as trapped high in a eucalyptus.

clue.text: One of the sisterhood gets a dance

definitions.meaning: a member of a lay religious community of women in the medieval Low Countries
a Caribbean ballroom dance similar to the rumba

explanation.surface: A nun takes to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beguines were medieval lay sisters living in community; the beguine is also a dance from Martinique.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay sister of a medieval women's community; also a bolero-like rhythm from the French Caribbean.

clue.text: Member of the family, Rex, involved in fuss

indicators.note: the king's letter is caught up inside the word for a fuss

parts.note: making a fuss is making a bother
R is the abbreviation of Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A relative called Rex is caught up in a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts R (Rex, king) inside BOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling is a close relation.

clue.text: Something intoxicating poured out in an hotel

indicators.note: the letters of an hotel are spilt and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A strong drink is served in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poured out' signals rearranging AN HOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The alcohol in beer, wine and spirits, which makes people drunk.

clue.text: Rumour about wine coming from the douro valley

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

parts.words: wine coming from the douro valley
parts.note: port is the fortified wine produced in Portugal's Douro valley

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning a Portuguese wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is made only from grapes grown in the Douro valley of northern Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay or common talk, as in 'by report he is rich'.

clue.text: Wait a short time before nurse appears

parts.note: T is the abbreviation of time
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hang on a moment before the nurse comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait' here means wait upon or serve, as a servant attends a master.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve someone, as in waiting on or looking after them.

clue.text: Garden item mum put on board (overgrew outside unfortunately)

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the board-and-mum pair
overgrew is unfortunately rearranged into a new order
in an across clue, mum goes on after board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A gardener's mother placed something on the table, with sad remarks about plants growing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of 'overgrew'; 'outside' splits the result around the board-and-mum pair, and 'put on' sets mum after board. A vegetable marrow is a big squash.
explanation.definitionFit: A large green squash grown in vegetable plots, much prized at British garden shows.

clue.text: Being less bright, faded around 2000

indicators.note: the word for faded wraps around the Roman numerals

parts.note: something that faded away died
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them make two thousand

explanation.surface: Something lost its brightness and faded at about the turn of the millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'approximately' but is the container signal; M is Roman 1000.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights that are turned down have reduced brightness.

clue.text: The German keeps behind, being more stupid

indicators.note: the German article holds the other word inside it

parts.note: der is a German word for the
aft means behind or towards the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A German man stays back, looking ever more foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is the container signal; aft is a nautical word for towards the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a colloquial word for silly or foolish.

clue.text: One putting on an exhibition in rain around the home counties

indicators.note: the word for heavy rain goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: when it rains heavily it pours
SE, the south-east of England, where the home counties around London lie

explanation.surface: An exhibitor stands in the rain somewhere near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the south-east; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off who acts affectedly to impress others is putting on a display.

clue.text: Part of machine that's quiet and almost completely hidden

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: nearly all of the word for hidden is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: something latent is present but hidden

explanation.surface: A machine component that is silent and nearly invisible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' drops the last letter of the word for hidden; p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The roller in a typewriter or the plate in a printing press that presses paper against the type.

clue.text: Female emerging from a scrap or two?

definitions.text: Female emerging from a scrap or two?

parts.words: Female emerging from a scrap or two?
parts.note: a girl figure that comes into being when a few cloth scraps are sewn together, not a woman coming out of a fight

explanation.surface: A woman stepping out of a fight or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a brawl, but here means a scrap of cloth: the toy is stitched from fabric remnants.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft toy figure made of stitched cloth remnants, often a girl.

clue.text: Mrs Joyce used to be a goose

definitions.meaning: James Joyce's wife, born in Galway
her maiden name was Barnacle, which is also a kind of goose, so before marriage she was a goose by name

explanation.surface: Someone claims a writer's wife was formerly a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce's wife was born a Barnacle; the barnacle goose is a species of wild goose, so she 'used to be' one.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of James Joyce's wife, whose maiden surname was that of a goose species.

clue.text: Remarkable penalty

definitions.meaning: a sum of money paid as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Excellent or of high quality; also a monetary punishment such as a parking charge.

clue.text: Minor reproof on leaving

indicators.note: the word on departs from the word for a reproof

parts.note: a rebuke that teaches someone a lesson
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small telling-off on someone's way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ON from LESSON, as in 'that'll teach you a lesson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smaller or inferior in importance, as in 'no less a person than'.

clue.text: Like someone on the way who is savvy?

definitions.meaning: '-wise' means in the manner of, so in the manner of one on the road

explanation.surface: Describing a wise traveller who knows the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix '-wise' means 'in the manner of', so the word can read as 'in the manner of the road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and experienced in coping with urban life; read as a split, in the manner of the road.

clue.text: Indications of kisses from old lovers?

definitions.meaning: the letter X written at the end of a note means a kiss, so several of them

explanation.surface: Kiss marks written to people one used to love.
explanation.walkthrough: An X at the foot of a letter stands for a kiss; the plural of the letter is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the spelt-out letter X; also former spouses or partners.

clue.text: People to give out prizes — TV personalities?

definitions.meaning: those who hand over awards at a ceremony

explanation.surface: Award-givers who are also celebrities from the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who hand over awards; also the hosts of broadcast shows.
